text:
maria: FYI I'm seeing reproducible OKHttp call cancellations during exponential backoff in our Kotlin SDK sampleapp on Android 14. Repro steps and logs below.

maria: Repro setup: Retrofit + OkHttp + custom RetryInterceptor (schedules coroutine delays for backoff), WorkManager enqueueExact for background sync, tokens via AuthInterceptor that may trigger refresh on 401. Happens reliably when device locks and network flaps.

maria: Relevant log snippet:
```
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
W/OkHttp: callTimedOut: canceling
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: canceled
E/SampleApp: TokenRefresh: started
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized
E/SampleApp: AuthInterceptor: refresh ok
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: canceled
```

maria: Notice two canceled calls and an auth refresh between them. The backoff coroutine seems to be canceling the pending OkHttp call somehow (or the call gets garbage-collected).

alex: Can you paste the RetryInterceptor? Does it wrap the OkHttp call or run the retry outside the Call lifecycle?

maria: Sure — simplified:
```kotlin
class RetryInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    var attempt = 0
    while (true) {
      try {
        return chain.proceed(chain.request())
      } catch (e: IOException) {
        if (attempt++ >= MAX) throw e
        runBlocking { delay(backoffMs(attempt)) } // naive backoff in interceptor
      }
    }
  }
}
```

maria: I know runBlocking in interceptor is questionable. In the real app we used a suspend-friendly implementation via a coroutineScope in a CallAdapter that schedules delays, but the simplified sample used runBlocking to reproduce quickly.

ben: runBlocking inside interceptor is going to block dispatcher threads. Also if Retrofit is using a coroutine call adapter that cancels the coroutine when the outer scope cancels, it will call OkHttp Call.cancel(). If your retry delay runs on the main thread or a shared dispatcher, cancellation can race with the next request.

ciara: Could also be WorkManager lifecycle. If the worker is stopped by OS while waiting during backoff, Worker.cancel gets propagated and might cancel coroutines which then cancel the OkHttp call. On API 34 we've seen more aggressive job preemption.

alex: Two suggestions: 1) don’t block inside Interceptor — use non-blocking suspend pattern in the CallAdapter or manage retries at Retrofit layer. 2) wrap OkHttp call in suspendCancellableCoroutine to ensure explicit cancellation semantics. Example:
```kotlin
suspend fun Call.awaitResponse(): Response = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  enqueue(object : Callback {
    override fun onFailure(call: Call, e: IOException) { if (!cont.isCancelled) cont.resumeWithException(e) }
    override fun onResponse(call: Call, r: Response) { if (!cont.isCancelled) cont.resume(r) }
  })
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
}
```

alex: That pattern makes cancellation explicit and avoids background delays inadvertently canceling the wrong Call. Also add an EventListener factory to log call start/end to see ordering.

maria: Good pointers. In our real implementation we do use enqueue + suspendCancellableCoroutine but the retry logic lives in a CallAdapter that cancels and resubmits Calls between attempts. I think when auth refresh runs it returns a new token and the previous Call gets canceled, but the next Call then immediately sees a different connection state and OkHttp reports "canceled" instead of failing cleanly.

nate: Quick thought — are you reusing the same Request object? Headers mutated between retries could confuse connection reuse. Also ensure retry uses newRequest = original.newBuilder().header("Authorization", token).build() before newCall.

maria: We do rebuild the request each attempt. I added EventListener logs and saw this ordering: callStart(A) -> callFailed(A) canceled -> callStart(B) -> response(B) 401 -> tokenRefresh -> callStart(C) -> canceled(C) -> callFailed(C) canceled. Looks like some internal connection pipeline cancels C after token refresh even though we start it after refresh.

ciara: That smells like connection coalescing or multiplexing (HTTP/2) where the connection state gets reset when auth header changes. Try disabling HTTP/2 in OkHttp client for a quick test (protocols = listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1)) and see if it stops.

maria: Will try. Also creating a tiny repro branch with WorkManager + foreground service to hit this on a Pixel 8 on Android 14. Push coming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/84 — please take a look. :eyes:

ben: Nice. Add a test that toggles dispatcher (IO vs Default) and a variant that uses Handler.postDelayed for backoff to compare.

alex: If disabling HTTP/2 fixes it, we should document a recommended pattern: don't cancel/recreate Calls concurrently on same connection with changing auth header; instead perform auth refresh and then retry from a single coroutine that serializes attempts. Also follow OkHttp recommended suspend wrapper.

maria: Plan: 1) add EventListener traces and HTTP/2 toggle in repro 2) try non-blocking suspend backoff and serialize retry loop 3) test on Android 13/14 devices 4) PR with fix and small note in SDK docs about WorkManager/foreground interactions.

maria: If anyone has quick suggestions for small experiments to pinpoint whether connectivity or coroutine cancellation is the root cause, shout. :pray:

alex: Try forcing a network drop (adb shell svc wifi disable) while waiting in backoff to reproduce. Also run with okhttp logger at BODY level.

ciara: I'll try repro on a Pixel 8 and report. If we confirm HTTP/2 interplay, we should add a test in CI that runs sampleapp on emulator image for Android 14.
